hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker handled batches normally (#817, #823) until it hit msg-811112 at offset 567980. Processing that message overflows the stack in expandReferences (likely a self-referencing or cyclic payload), which is an unhandled RangeError that kills the process (#825). Each restart picks up again at the same committed offset (#909), crashes on the same message (#844, #870), and the restart backoff grows (10s, 20s, 40s). That is the CrashLoopBackOff, and it is why lag on notifications.outbound keeps rising. The worker ran v4.29.0 on every restart and processed messages fine before this one, so a deploy doesn't explain it. Upstream services (notification-svc, template-svc, gateway) show no errors.
report-cron:2026.10.2 is missing pandas, so its revenue-report job keeps failing. This is a separate problem and has nothing to do with notif-worker or the notifications queue.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-811112 (offset 567980) off notifications.outbound to a dead-letter queue, or skip it by committing offset 567981, so the worker can drain the backlog. Then fix expandReferences: detect cycles and limit recursion depth. Also catch per-message exceptions and send failing messages to a DLQ instead of crashing the process. Separately, fix the report-cron image so it includes pandas.
